<!-- PR conventions checked in CI:
Use a Conventional Commits title (for example, "fix: correct validation").
Write the first # heading exactly as
# [REPO#NUMBER](https://github.com/Rubio-Enterprises/REPO/issues/NUMBER)
(use /pull/ instead of /issues/ for a PR), replacing REPO and NUMBER with matching values,
or write # No associated work item.
What?, Why?, How?, and Testing? are required ## headings with non-empty content.
The remaining sections are optional. Keep the description to at most 400 words;
HTML comments are excluded, link text and code count, and link URLs do not.
-->
<!-- pr-conventions: {"required": ["What?", "Why?", "How?", "Testing?"], "maxWords": 400} -->
# [REPO#NUMBER](https://github.com/Rubio-Enterprises/REPO/issues/NUMBER)

## What?

<!-- What does this PR change? Describe the overall effect in a few concise sentences. Do not rely only on the PR title or a linked issue. -->

## Why?

<!-- Why is this change needed? Explain the user, business, or engineering problem it addresses. Link any related issues, tickets, design documents, or prior discussions. -->

## How?

<!-- How does the change work? Call out important implementation details, design decisions, trade-offs, and limitations that are not obvious from the diff. -->

## Testing?

<!-- How was the change verified? Describe automated and manual testing, relevant edge cases, and any scenarios that were not tested. Note any associated risks. -->

## Feedback?

<!-- What should reviewers focus on? Call out specific decisions, concerns, or questions on which feedback would be especially useful. -->

## Other Information or Known Dependencies

<!-- Include any additional context, known dependencies, rollout considerations, required configuration changes, related deployments, or follow-up work. -->

## Screenshots (optional)

<!-- Include before-and-after screenshots or relevant output for visual or behavioral changes. -->
